following the 2024 launch of the church’s child safeguarding policy, ailish higgins, our diocesan director of safeguarding met with young people from the diocese to ask them “what does a safe & welcoming church mean to you?” thanks to all the children and young people who took part in these sessions and were open and honest about their experience of parish life. thanks too to their parents, the group leaders and parish priests who supported the facilitation of these groups. national board for safeguarding children in the catholic church in ireland – biannual conference the held their biannual conference from 3rd – 5th september 2025 titled: towards a restorative and transitional justice model of engaging with victims and survivors in the catholic church in ireland. the event aimed to enhance the understanding we all have of how we must engage in a just and restorative way with those who have suffered harm in the catholic church in ireland. our diocesan director of safeguarding and dlp attended the event and shared valuable feedback with our diocesan safeguarding committee. the learning from the conference will help guide our practice going forward. special thanks to the national board for organising and hosting the event. youth participation amadeus christmas clane confirmation class safeguarding checklist for parishes displayed in all church porches the kildare & junior infants enrolment – september 2027 enrolment is now open for junior infants commencing in september 2027 in our cathedr al parish primary schools: st joseph’s national school , scoil mhuire gan smál parents and guardians wishing to enrol their children are warmly invited to contact their p referred school for further information and enrolment details. the irish cancer society is seeking compassionate volunteer drivers as a volunteer driver you would be bringing patients undergoing che motherapy to the hospital and back home for their treatment. gifting your time means that cancer patients will have comfortable (one on one) transport to attend appointments for their lifesaving treatment. if you can spare 2 days per month, have a valid driving licence, and a safe, reli able vehicle, you are the perfect candidate to make a significant difference. the irish cancer socie ty will provide you with training before you start as a driver for us. your generosity not only eases the journey many during a challenging time but also offers comfort and support when it's needed most. for more information and to become a volunteer driver, please contact monica or emily at
volunteer@irishcancer.ie
